We derive a set of equations that describe the behavior of the gravitational field in this regime, and use them to investigate the properties of the gravitational field in the vicinity of a binary system. Our results show that the gravitational field in this regime can be described by a set of linear equations that are similar to those found in classical electrodynamics. We also find that the gravitational field in this regime is dominated by the mass and angular momentum of the binary system, and that the effects of the gravitational field on the motion of the binary components can be neglected. Our findings provide a useful starting point for developing more accurate models of binary systems in the strong-field regime.

In this study, we utilize angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to investigate the FeSe$_{0.9}$Te$_{0.1}$ thin film, which exhibits a multiband superconducting gap structure. Our analysis reveals two distinct gap features: a large gap of approximately 4.5 meV in the hole-like bands and a smaller gap of around 1.5 meV in the electron-like bands. Instead, our results support the concept of an unconventional superconducting gap structure that is determined by the superconducting pairing symmetry.
